findings.reason: a node implementing the assertion as written either pegs it to a route whose payload has no blocked/not-blocked value (an assertion that cannot fail, the very defect the node exists to exclude) or must substitute the inventory surface the plan never names, so the third leg of the agreement check is either vacuous or unnamed.
findings.text: §3's done-when asserts that "`roadmap`, the `/plan` route in `serve.py` and `read_plan` agree on every fixture, because all three read the one function", but `GET /plan/<project>/<slug>` returns `_plan_html.parse_plan(pf)` output with no `blocking`, `effective_status` or readiness field (`reckon/serve.py:3108-3111`), so there is nothing in that response for a fixture to agree or disagree with; the serve.py reader of `split_unpassed_gates` is at `reckon/serve.py:1924` inside `_derive_lifecycle` (`reckon/serve.py:1840`), which is reached from plan discovery (`reckon/serve.py:1599`, `1667`) and served on `/state/<project>/index.json`, not the `/plan` route

findings.reason: §2's closable test runs before the readiness ladder reaches `blocked`, so such a plan reads `closable` with the gate listed in `closure_blockers` either way, and §1's census exercises no section-less gate among the three blocked plans.
findings.text: §3 states the no-gated-sections case only for "a plan that still has implementable work", leaving unsettled what an open, section-less gate does to a finished plan, where today it holds the plan outright (the function docstring: "A gate that names no sections always holds the plan", `reckon/roadmap.py:799`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `split_unpassed_gates` (`reckon/roadmap.py:789`, body call at 807), the ladder (`reckon/roadmap.py:3200`), `serve.py:1924`, `reckon/mcp_views.py:2490` with `_section_gate_blockers` at `reckon/mcp_views.py:2504`, and `unpassed_gate_blockers(gates)` (`reckon/lifecycle.py:52`) all resolve and carry the shapes §3 states; the `_plan_gate_blockers` symbol the previous review rejected is gone.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's agreement assertion names the `/plan` route in `serve.py`, which serves raw parsed plan state and carries no blocking or readiness field.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the census, the roadmap reads and their output sit on the durable, committed path `docs/evidence/archive/a-finished-plan-closes-landed.html`, cited from §1 and the source of the three blocked plans' rows.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §3 introduces no symbol of its own, and every name it uses for the target and its readers is the name the code uses, with no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause reproduces (a closed gate with verdict `failed` is unpassed, so it holds: `_gate_verdict` writes `status: "closed"`, `verdict: "failed"` at `reckon/_store.py:3264`, and `unpassed_gate_blockers` keeps verdicts other than `passed`), and `split_unpassed_gates` is the reader the three blocked plans' `gate_blockers` rows come from, so §3's rules unblock all three §1 shapes (open gate on done `s8`; open gate on deferred `s11`; closed failed gate).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 carries one deliverable: one edit to `split_unpassed_gates` in `reckon/roadmap.py`.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §3 needs no declared edge (its mechanism is self-contained), the map resolves s5→s2 for §5's wait on §2's closing list, and s6 holds on s2–s5 through `plan-section-depends-on` in the snapshot's `<meta>` block.
